title: Abu Dhabi court grants Binance $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order over October 29 theft
date_note: The day Binance announced the order: The Block (18 November) says Binance said it Wednesday in a statement. No page read gives the day the court granted the order; Nairametrics refers to a Binance statement dated 20 November.
place: Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts, Abu Dhabi
geo_basis: the issuing court (Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts) as the sources state
summary: Binance said the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts granted it a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order, issued by Justice William Stone against unidentified persons behind its October 29 security incident. Binance's lawyers Gibson Dunn said a 'living list' of 26,000 wallet addresses holds stolen assets. The Block reports Binance had earlier said about $2.85 billion of roughly $6.34 billion affected was frozen or intercepted.
plain: A court in Abu Dhabi let Binance freeze up to $6.5 billion worldwide as it tries to get back crypto stolen in its October 29 hack. The thieves are not named.
exec: A $6.5 billion freezing order gives Binance a legal route to recover stolen crypto held in 26,000 wallet addresses its lawyers listed.

evidence.quote: The amount of the injunction is $6.5 billion, making it perhaps the largest publicly known such order ever made.
a constantly updating 'living list' of 26,000 wallet addresses identified as holding stolen assets
about $2.85 billion of the roughly $6.34 billion in assets affected by the hack had been frozen or intercepted

validation.note: The Block and Gulf Today each report Binance's statement on the $6.5 billion ADGM order by Justice William Stone; Nairametrics repeats it. Binance's own announcement was not linked by any of them and was not read. The $2.85 billion figure is from The Block only.
